Washington, Tuesday, January 8, 1946
The President
EXECUTIVE ORDER 9674 
Liquidation  op W ar A gencies
By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Constitution and statutes, includ­
ing Title I of the First War Powers Act, 
1941 (55 Stat. 838), and as President of 
the United States, it is hereby ordered 
as follows:
1. There shall be in the Office for 
Emergency Management of the Execu­
tive Office of the President a Director of 
Liquidation, hereinafter referred to as 
the Director, who shall be appointed by 
the President and who shall perform his 
functions in consultation with a Liqui­
dation Advisory Committee.
The Liquidation Advisory Committee 
shall be composed of one representative 
of each of the following agencies: the 
Department of the Treasury, the Sur­
plus Property Administration, the Na­
tional Archives, the Civil Service Com­
mission, the Public Buildings Adminis­
tration, the General Accounting Office, 
and the Bureau of the Budget. The 
chairman of the Committee shall be 
designated by the Director from the 
Committee’ s membership.
2. It shall be the duty of the Director 
to further proper preparations, arrange­
ments, and methods for the orderly and 
timely winding up of the affairs of the 
temporary Federal agencies created for 
the purposes of the war, hereinafter re­
ferred to as war agencies, particularly 
with respect to personnel, property, ac­
counts, space, and records. To this end 
the Director shall:
(a) Cause to be developed by each war 
agency, for use whenever it shall, pur­
suant to Act of Congress or order of the 
President, as the case may be, cease the 
performance of its substantive functions 
or . materially reduce the volume of its 
activities, suitable plans for the winding 
up or retrenchment of its affairs.
(b) When deemed appropriate, ar­
range for the designation, by the head 
of any war agency, of a liquidation of­
ficer for the agency.
(c) Receive periodic reports which 
.be submitted by each war agency,
showing the status of preparation for 
liquidation, or of liquidation, as the case may be.
(d) Establish such uniform liquida­
tion practices as will accelerate the rate 
or improve the quality of the liquidation.
(e) Suggest to the Civil Service Com­
mission and the Liaison Officer for Per­
sonnel Management measures designed 
to ameliorate the impact of liquidation 
upon the employees of the war agencies 
liquidated.
(f) Advise and assist the war agencies 
in such other respects as will facilitate 
the preparation for and the carrying 
out of the liquidation of their affairs.
3. Nothing in this order shall be 
deemed to divest any agency referred to 
in paragraph 1 of this order of any of 
its functions which may be concerned 
with the liquidation of a war agency. 
The functions of the Director shall not 
be deemed to extend to the affairs of 
any agency which has heretofore been, 
or shall hereafter be, abolished and the 
affairs of which are transferred to the 
Department of the Treasury, or to any 
other department, for the final winding 
up of such affairs. -
4. The Director may, within the limits 
of funds which may be made available, 
employ personnel and make provisions 
for supplies, facilities, and services, and 
incur other expenses, necessary to dis­
charge the functions of the Director un­
der this order.
Harry S. T ruman
The W hite  H ouse,
January 4, 1946.

research_rationale:
EO 9674 (January 4, 1946) created a Director of Liquidation and a Liquidation Advisory Committee in the Office for Emergency Management to further the winding up of the war agencies. It has no own-terms sunset. EO 9744 of June 27, 1946 provides that the office of the Director of Liquidation and the Liquidation Advisory Committee, established by Executive Order No. 9674, together with their functions, "are hereby terminated", and states that it becomes effective on June 30, 1946. The status is NO: the bodies and every function the order gave them were terminated effective June 30, 1946, and no held source revives them.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No own-terms end: EO 9674 states no date, condition or sunset for the Director or the Committee. The held number search found only EO 9744 (and a duplicate Federal Register page that reprints it) acting on EO 9674; the OFR catalog note naming EO 9744 (June 27, 1946) as the revoking order agrees with the held text. No earlier abolition of this Office is shown by a held source. Paragraph 3 of the order says the Director's functions do not reach agencies already abolished, which limits his reach but ends no clause.","independent_command_check":"Each clause is a continuing duty or authority of the Director or the Committee, or a limiting rule on them, with no performance date in the order. No held source shows any of them performed or exhausted before June 30, 1946, so the stated effective termination is the first established end of each.","savings_check":"EO 9744 directs the Director of the Bureau of the Budget, consonant with applicable law, to make suitable disposition of the records and property in the possession of the Director of Liquidation. That residual disposition duty is a new command of EO 9744, not a continuation of EO 9674, and no held source preserves any other EO 9674 clause.","scope_check":"EO 9744 terminates the office of the Director of Liquidation and the Liquidation Advisory Committee together with the functions of the Director and the Committee, which are exactly what paragraphs 1, 2(a)-(f), 3 and 4 of EO 9674 create or limit, so every clause ends. The termination is stated as effective June 30, 1946 (signing June 27, 1946)."}

That residual disposition duty is a new command of EO 9744, not a continuation of EO 9674, and no held source preserves any other EO 9674 clause.
